Manage docs: a project's text, kept by wdx outside its repository.

A doc belongs to a project and is there for every person and agent as soon as it is written. Every change of its content is a new revision, made on the revision it was read at: get a copy with doc get `--out`, change it, and write it back with doc update `--base`. Its status says whether it is agreed on: wip, review, approved or rejected; changing its content makes it wip.

Its folder, such as /hub/initial, is only where tide shows it, / for the top: a folder given is cleaned (whitespace dropped, lowercased, one / between its parts and at its start) and then has a-z, 0-9, \_, - and / only. Names stay unique within a project whatever the folder.

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| [`wdx doc create`](#wdx-doc-create) | Create a doc, from a file or empty |
| [`wdx doc get`](#wdx-doc-get) | Print a doc's content, or write it to a file to change |
| [`wdx doc history`](#wdx-doc-history) | List a doc's revisions |
| [`wdx doc list`](#wdx-doc-list) | List a project's docs |
| [`wdx doc remove`](#wdx-doc-remove) | Delete a doc and all its revisions |
| [`wdx doc rename`](#wdx-doc-rename) | Rename a doc |
| [`wdx doc set`](#wdx-doc-set) | Change a doc's folder, status or labels |
| [`wdx doc sync-to-git`](#wdx-doc-sync-to-git) | Write a project's docs, read-only, into a directory of its repository |
| [`wdx doc update`](#wdx-doc-update) | Write a doc's content as a new revision |

## wdx doc create

Create a doc, from a file or empty.

```sh
wdx doc create [--project-id <id> | --project-name <name>] [--name <name>] [--path <file> | --path -] [--folder <folder>] [--format <ext>] [--labels <a,b>] [--status <status>] [flags]
```

Its content is the file `--path` names, stdin with `--path` -, or nothing. The name is the file's without its extension unless `--name` is given, and is required without a file; names have letters, numbers, \_ and - only, and are unique within a project whatever their case. The format, the extension its copies get, is the file's, else md. Labels have lowercase letters, numbers, \_ and - only. Content is UTF-8 text of at most 2 MiB.

A name the project has is refused: changing a doc's content is doc update.

### Flags

| Flag | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--folder <folder>` |  | folder tide shows it in, such as /hub/initial (default: /, the top) |
| `--format <extension>` |  | extension of its copies, such as md or txt (default: the file's, else md) |
| `--labels <labels>` | `[]` | labels to give it, comma-separated |
| `--name <name>` |  | name of the doc (default: the file's, without its extension) |
| `--path <file>` |  | file to take the content from, - for stdin (default: empty) |
| `--project-id <id>` |  | id of the project (default: the one the working directory is in) |
| `--project-name <name>` |  | name of the project (default: the one the working directory is in) |
| `--status <status>` |  | status to create it in: wip, review, approved or rejected (default: wip) |

- at most one of `--project-id` or `--project-name`

### Examples

```sh
# Add a file of the project you are in as a doc
wdx doc create --path docs/auth.md

# Name it, label it and pick the project
wdx doc create --project-name app --path notes.md --name auth-rfc --labels auth,rfc

# In a folder
wdx doc create --path docs/auth.md --folder /hub/initial

# From stdin, as JSON
wdx doc create --name auth-rfc --path - --status review --json
```

### Output

The doc, at revision 1. With `--json`: {"result": "created", "doc": {...}}

With `--json`, `result` is one of: `created`.

### Errors

| Code | Exit | When |
|---|---|---|
| [`daemon_unavailable`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#daemon_unavailable) | 3 | the daemon is not running or not answering |
| [`invalid_argument`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#invalid_argument) | 1 | an argument is empty or malformed |
| [`invalid_name`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#invalid_name) | 1 | the name is not allowed |
| [`name_taken`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#name_taken) | 1 | something else has this name |
| [`not_found`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#not_found) | 1 | nothing has this name or id |
| [`usage`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#usage) | 2 | the request, command line or a setting is invalid |
| [`internal`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#internal) | 3 | an unexpected failure: database, filesystem or git |

## wdx doc get

Print a doc's content, or write it to a file to change.

```sh
wdx doc get (--id <id> | --name <name>) [--project-id <id> | --project-name <name>] [--revision <n>] [--out <file> [--overwrite]] [flags]
```

The latest revision unless `--revision` is given, printed byte for byte, as cat does. With `--out` it is written to a file of yours to edit, then given back with doc update `--base` and the revision it was read at; a file there is replaced only with `--overwrite`.

### Flags

| Flag | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--id <id>` |  | id of the doc |
| `--name <name>` |  | name of the doc (case-insensitive) |
| `--out <file>` |  | file to write it to, read-write, instead of printing it |
| `--overwrite` |  | with `--out`, replace the file if there is one |
| `--project-id <id>` |  | id of the project (default: the one the working directory is in) |
| `--project-name <name>` |  | name of the project (default: the one the working directory is in) |
| `--revision <revision>` | `0` | the revision to get (default: the latest) |

- exactly one of `--id` or `--name`
- at most one of `--project-id` or `--project-name`

### Examples

```sh
# Print a doc of the project you are in
wdx doc get --name auth-rfc

# Write it to a file to change
wdx doc get --name auth-rfc --out auth-rfc.md

# Get it again after it changed
wdx doc get --name auth-rfc --out auth-rfc.md --overwrite

# An earlier revision, as JSON
wdx doc get --id doc-1a2b3c4d --revision 3 --json
```

### Output

The content alone; with `--out`, the revision written and where. With `--json`: {"doc": {...}, "revision": ..., "content": "..."}, without content with `--out`

### Errors

| Code | Exit | When |
|---|---|---|
| [`daemon_unavailable`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#daemon_unavailable) | 3 | the daemon is not running or not answering |
| [`not_found`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#not_found) | 1 | nothing has this name or id |
| [`path_exists`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#path_exists) | 1 | something is already at the path, as the directory to clone into |
| [`usage`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#usage) | 2 | the request, command line or a setting is invalid |
| [`internal`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#internal) | 3 | an unexpected failure: database, filesystem or git |

## wdx doc history

List a doc's revisions.

```sh
wdx doc history (--id <id> | --name <name>) [--project-id <id> | --project-name <name>] [flags]
```

Every revision is kept until the doc is removed; doc get `--revision` reads one.

### Flags

| Flag | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--id <id>` |  | id of the doc |
| `--name <name>` |  | name of the doc (case-insensitive) |
| `--project-id <id>` |  | id of the project (default: the one the working directory is in) |
| `--project-name <name>` |  | name of the project (default: the one the working directory is in) |

- exactly one of `--id` or `--name`
- at most one of `--project-id` or `--project-name`

### Examples

```sh
# The revisions of a doc of the project you are in
wdx doc history --name auth-rfc

# By id, as JSON
wdx doc history --id doc-1a2b3c4d --json
```

### Output

The revisions, latest first, without content. With `--json`: {"revisions": [...]}

### Errors

| Code | Exit | When |
|---|---|---|
| [`daemon_unavailable`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#daemon_unavailable) | 3 | the daemon is not running or not answering |
| [`not_found`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#not_found) | 1 | nothing has this name or id |
| [`usage`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#usage) | 2 | the request, command line or a setting is invalid |
| [`internal`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#internal) | 3 | an unexpected failure: database, filesystem or git |

## wdx doc list

List a project's docs.

```sh
wdx doc list [--project-id <id> | --project-name <name>] [--labels <a,b>] [--status <status>] [flags]
```

Without a project flag, the docs of the project the working directory is in. With `--labels`, only those that have every one of them.

### Flags

| Flag | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--labels <labels>` | `[]` | labels a doc must all have, comma-separated |
| `--project-id <id>` |  | id of the project (default: the one the working directory is in) |
| `--project-name <name>` |  | name of the project (default: the one the working directory is in) |
| `--status <status>` |  | the status a doc must be in |

- at most one of `--project-id` or `--project-name`

### Examples

```sh
# The docs of the project you are in
wdx doc list

# The approved docs labeled auth, as JSON
wdx doc list --project-name app --labels auth --status approved --json
```

### Output

The docs by folder, then name, without content; an empty list when there are none. With `--json`: {"docs": [...]}

### Errors

| Code | Exit | When |
|---|---|---|
| [`daemon_unavailable`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#daemon_unavailable) | 3 | the daemon is not running or not answering |
| [`invalid_argument`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#invalid_argument) | 1 | an argument is empty or malformed |
| [`not_found`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#not_found) | 1 | nothing has this name or id |
| [`usage`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#usage) | 2 | the request, command line or a setting is invalid |
| [`internal`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#internal) | 3 | an unexpected failure: database, filesystem or git |

## wdx doc remove

Delete a doc and all its revisions.

```sh
wdx doc remove (--id <id> | --name <name>) [--project-id <id> | --project-name <name>] [--yes] [flags]
```

You are asked first, as nothing brings it back; `--yes` answers in advance, and with `--json`, or without a terminal, it is required.

### Flags

| Flag | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--id <id>` |  | id of the doc |
| `--name <name>` |  | name of the doc (case-insensitive) |
| `--project-id <id>` |  | id of the project (default: the one the working directory is in) |
| `--project-name <name>` |  | name of the project (default: the one the working directory is in) |
| `--yes` |  | remove it without asking |

- exactly one of `--id` or `--name`
- at most one of `--project-id` or `--project-name`
- with `--json`: one of `--yes`

### Examples

```sh
# Remove a doc of the project you are in
wdx doc remove --name auth-rfc

# From a script
wdx doc remove --id doc-1a2b3c4d --yes --json
```

### Output

The removed doc, as it was before. With `--json`: {"result": "removed", "doc": {...}}

With `--json`, `result` is one of: `removed`.

### Errors

| Code | Exit | When |
|---|---|---|
| [`cancelled`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#cancelled) | 1 | the question was answered no |
| [`daemon_unavailable`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#daemon_unavailable) | 3 | the daemon is not running or not answering |
| [`not_found`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#not_found) | 1 | nothing has this name or id |
| [`usage`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#usage) | 2 | the request, command line or a setting is invalid |
| [`internal`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#internal) | 3 | an unexpected failure: database, filesystem or git |

## wdx doc rename

Rename a doc.

```sh
wdx doc rename (--id <id> | --name <name>) [--project-id <id> | --project-name <name>] --new-name <name> [flags]
```

Its id, content, revisions and status stay as they are; changing only the case of its name is a rename.

### Flags

| Flag | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--id <id>` |  | id of the doc |
| `--name <name>` |  | name of the doc (case-insensitive) |
| `--new-name <name>` |  | the doc's new name |
| `--project-id <id>` |  | id of the project (default: the one the working directory is in) |
| `--project-name <name>` |  | name of the project (default: the one the working directory is in) |

- `--new-name` is required
- exactly one of `--id` or `--name`
- at most one of `--project-id` or `--project-name`

### Examples

```sh
# Rename a doc of the project you are in
wdx doc rename --name auth-rfc --new-name auth-design

# By id, as JSON
wdx doc rename --id doc-1a2b3c4d --new-name auth-design --json
```

### Output

The doc's name before and now. With `--json`: {"result": "updated", "doc": {...}}

With `--json`, `result` is one of: `updated` or `unchanged`.

### Errors

| Code | Exit | When |
|---|---|---|
| [`daemon_unavailable`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#daemon_unavailable) | 3 | the daemon is not running or not answering |
| [`invalid_name`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#invalid_name) | 1 | the name is not allowed |
| [`name_taken`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#name_taken) | 1 | something else has this name |
| [`not_found`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#not_found) | 1 | nothing has this name or id |
| [`usage`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#usage) | 2 | the request, command line or a setting is invalid |
| [`internal`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#internal) | 3 | an unexpected failure: database, filesystem or git |

## wdx doc set

Change a doc's folder, status or labels.

```sh
wdx doc set (--id <id> | --name <name>) [--project-id <id> | --project-name <name>] [--folder <folder>] [--status <status>] [--add-labels <a,b>] [--remove-labels <a,b>] [flags]
```

Its content and revision stay as they are, and no base is needed. Removing a label it does not have is not an error.

### Flags

| Flag | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--add-labels <labels>` | `[]` | labels to add, comma-separated |
| `--folder <folder>` |  | folder to move it to, such as /hub/initial; / is the top |
| `--id <id>` |  | id of the doc |
| `--name <name>` |  | name of the doc (case-insensitive) |
| `--project-id <id>` |  | id of the project (default: the one the working directory is in) |
| `--project-name <name>` |  | name of the project (default: the one the working directory is in) |
| `--remove-labels <labels>` | `[]` | labels to remove, comma-separated |
| `--status <status>` |  | status to give it: wip, review, approved or rejected |

- at least one of `--folder`, `--status`, `--add-labels` or `--remove-labels`
- exactly one of `--id` or `--name`
- at most one of `--project-id` or `--project-name`

### Examples

```sh
# Approve a doc of the project you are in
wdx doc set --name auth-rfc --status approved

# Change its labels, as JSON
wdx doc set --id doc-1a2b3c4d --add-labels auth --remove-labels draft --json

# Move it to a folder
wdx doc set --name auth-rfc --folder /hub/initial
```

### Output

The doc's status, folder and labels now. With `--json`: {"result": "updated", "doc": {...}}

With `--json`, `result` is one of: `updated` or `unchanged`.

### Errors

| Code | Exit | When |
|---|---|---|
| [`daemon_unavailable`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#daemon_unavailable) | 3 | the daemon is not running or not answering |
| [`invalid_argument`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#invalid_argument) | 1 | an argument is empty or malformed |
| [`not_found`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#not_found) | 1 | nothing has this name or id |
| [`usage`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#usage) | 2 | the request, command line or a setting is invalid |
| [`internal`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#internal) | 3 | an unexpected failure: database, filesystem or git |

## wdx doc sync-to-git

Write a project's docs, read-only, into a directory of its repository.

```sh
wdx doc sync-to-git [--project-id <id> | --project-name <name>] --path <dir> [flags]
```

`--path` is relative to the project's main checkout, wherever this runs, and is created when missing. Each doc's latest revision is written as &lt;name&gt;.&lt;format&gt;; a file of that name that wdx did not write is left as it is. Files wdx wrote there of docs that are gone are removed, and only those: .wdx-docs lists what it wrote. Nothing is staged or committed. The setting docs.git\_path has the daemon do this on every change.

### Flags

| Flag | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--path <dir>` |  | dir to write into, relative to the project's main checkout |
| `--project-id <id>` |  | id of the project (default: the one the working directory is in) |
| `--project-name <name>` |  | name of the project (default: the one the working directory is in) |

- `--path` is required
- at most one of `--project-id` or `--project-name`

### Examples

```sh
# Write the docs of the project you are in
wdx doc sync-to-git --path docs/wdx

# Of another project, as JSON
wdx doc sync-to-git --project-name app --path docs/wdx --json
```

### Output

How many docs were written and where, and the files removed or skipped. With `--json`: {"result": "synced", "path": "...", "written": [...], "removed": [...], "skipped": [...]}

With `--json`, `result` is one of: `synced`.

### Errors

| Code | Exit | When |
|---|---|---|
| [`checkout_missing`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#checkout_missing) | 1 | none of the project's checkouts is left on disk |
| [`daemon_unavailable`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#daemon_unavailable) | 3 | the daemon is not running or not answering |
| [`invalid_path`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#invalid_path) | 1 | the path cannot be used |
| [`not_found`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#not_found) | 1 | nothing has this name or id |
| [`usage`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#usage) | 2 | the request, command line or a setting is invalid |
| [`internal`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#internal) | 3 | an unexpected failure: database, filesystem or git |

## wdx doc update

Write a doc's content as a new revision.

```sh
wdx doc update (--id <id> | --name <name>) [--project-id <id> | --project-name <name>] --path <file> --base <n> [flags]
```

`--base` is the revision the change was made on, as doc get printed it. If the doc has a newer revision, nothing is written: get it again, apply the change to it and update with the new base, so that no change is lost. A new revision makes the doc wip, whatever it was; content equal to the latest makes none and changes nothing.

### Flags

| Flag | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--base <revision>` | `0` | the revision the change was made on |
| `--id <id>` |  | id of the doc |
| `--name <name>` |  | name of the doc (case-insensitive) |
| `--path <file>` |  | file holding the new content, - for stdin |
| `--project-id <id>` |  | id of the project (default: the one the working directory is in) |
| `--project-name <name>` |  | name of the project (default: the one the working directory is in) |

- `--base` is required
- `--path` is required
- exactly one of `--id` or `--name`
- at most one of `--project-id` or `--project-name`

### Examples

```sh
# Write back a changed copy
wdx doc update --name auth-rfc --path auth-rfc.md --base 4

# From stdin, as JSON
wdx doc update --id doc-1a2b3c4d --path - --base 4 --json
```

### Output

The doc's revision now. With `--json`: {"result": "updated", "doc": {...}, "previous\_status": ...}

With `--json`, `result` is one of: `updated` or `unchanged`.

### Errors

| Code | Exit | When |
|---|---|---|
| [`daemon_unavailable`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#daemon_unavailable) | 3 | the daemon is not running or not answering |
| [`doc_changed`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#doc_changed) | 1 | the doc has a newer revision than the base given |
| [`invalid_argument`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#invalid_argument) | 1 | an argument is empty or malformed |
| [`not_found`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#not_found) | 1 | nothing has this name or id |
| [`usage`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#usage) | 2 | the request, command line or a setting is invalid |
| [`internal`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#internal) | 3 | an unexpected failure: database, filesystem or git |
